text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister candidate Andris Shkele completed the first round of consultations with six parties, potential members of the new coalition government. The factions have to agree on the draft declaration by Friday.

- Prime ministers of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia meet in Tallinn in a regular meeting of the Baltic Council of Ministers to discuss co-operaration issues, including the customs union and easing of transit procedures.
- Riga might be granted the status of the European cultural capital of 2001, the Culture Ministry says. The final decision is expected this year from the EU committee in charge of cultural affairs.
- Latvian Gas company announced it would lift tariffs unless Latvenergo and Riga Heat use more gas.
- Parliament has amended the law on fire arms, loosening the regulations on Latvian citizens bearing arms.
- Ventspils port has been put among Europe's top twelve ports in terms of cargo turnover. Last year the port handled 37.5 million tonnes, a 20 percent rise from 1995.
